content: This paper proposes a novel method for simultaneous feature selection and classification of longitudinal (functional) data with categorical outcomes, formulating a new optimization problem that combines logistic loss with functional features to identify the most discriminative features. By leveraging functional principal components and an adaptive Dual Augmented Lagrangian algorithm—designed to exploit sparsity—the approach achieves computational efficiency and scalability to high-dimensional settings (where features far outnumber samples), with strong performance validated via simulations and a real-world analysis of chronic disease associations with health and socio-demographic factors.
